mainTopic: הלל at the סדר, the wording of ברכה endings, and the third and fourth cups
overview: The amud opens by asking how far to say הלל before the meal at the סדר: until ״אם הבנים שמחה״, as the משנה says, or until ״בצאת ישראל״, as the ברייתא says. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא each show that the sources need not argue. Each reading strains one source's wording, and both end with a קשיא. Next, explaining 'וחותם בגאולה', רבא and רבי זירא teach that praise of the past uses past tense ('גאל ישראל', 'אשר קדשנו'), while תפילה, a request for mercy, uses request language. רב אחא בר יעקב teaches that קידוש must mention יציאת מצרים. The גמרא then gives sources for the endings 'מגן דוד' and 'מגן אברהם'. רבא disagrees with סבי דפומבדיתא about how תפילה and קידוש end on שבת and יום טוב. Stories about רבא, רב פפא and מרימר show that the הלכה follows סבי דפומבדיתא. Finally, a new משנה describes the third and fourth cups, and רבא rejects רב חנן's proof that ברכת המזון always needs a cup. The amud ends by quoting the משנה about ברכת השיר, which the next amud explains.

steps.title: Suggesting the two sources argue about where הללויה belongs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה and the ברייתא disagree about whether הללויה starts a chapter or ends one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they argue about? The one who says 'until ״אם הבנים שמחה״' holds that הללויה is the start of the next chapter. The one who says 'until ״בצאת ישראל״' holds that הללויה is the end of the earlier chapter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to use the difference between the משנה (until ״אם הבנים שמחה״) and the ברייתא (until ״בצאת ישראל״) as proof that there is a real argument about where הללויה belongs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse ״מושיבי עקרת הבית אם הבנים שמחה הללויה״ ends one chapter, and ״בצאת ישראל ממצרים״ starts the next. If you stop at ״אם הבנים שמחה״, you must think הללויה belongs to the next chapter, so you leave it out. If you go up to ״בצאת ישראל״, you must think הללויה belongs to the earlier chapter, so you include it.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (introduces a suggested proof)
the word 'Halleluyah' that sits between the two chapters

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides say the same verses. The only question is the single word הללויה: is it said now, before the meal, or later, when הלל resumes after the meal?

phrases.english: What, is it not that they argue about this:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is trying to prove something from their argument.

phrases.english: According to the one who says 'until "A joyful mother of children"',
phrases.notes: This is how the משנה puts it.

phrases.english: he holds that 'Halleluyah' is the start of a chapter,
and the one who says 'until "When Israel came forth"',
phrases.notes: This is how the ברייתא puts it.

phrases.english: holds that 'Halleluyah' is the end of a chapter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the earlier contrast between the משנה and the ברייתא about the stopping point of הלל.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a real argument over whether הללויה starts or ends a chapter.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The differing stopping points in the משנה (״אם הבנים שמחה״) and the ברייתא (״בצאת ישראל״).

steps.title: רב חסדא: everyone agrees הללויה ends a chapter
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא reads both sources as agreeing that הללויה is the end of a chapter, explaining 'until' as 'until and including.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא explains it according to his own view: everyone holds that הללויה is the end of a chapter. The one who says 'until ״בצאת ישראל״' is fine. The one who says 'until ״אם הבנים שמחה״' means 'until, and including the word after it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggested proof. רב חסדא shows that both sources can agree that הללויה ends the earlier chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב חסדא, the ברייתא's 'until ״בצאת ישראל״' works perfectly: you finish everything before that, including הללויה. The משנה's 'until ״אם הבנים שמחה״' must then mean 'including the rest of that verse,' which covers the word הללויה. So there is no real argument.

keyTerms.meaning: explains it according to his own known view

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common גמרא move: an apparent argument disappears once the word 'עד' (until) is read as including or excluding the end point.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda explains it according to his reasoning,
that everyone holds:
'Halleluyah' is the end of a chapter.
The one who says 'until "When Israel came forth"' is fine,
and the one who says 'until "A joyful mother of children"',
means 'until', and the end point is included.
phrases.notes: So the word הללויה is said as well

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 1's claim that the sources must disagree.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that the משנה and the ברייתא argue.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'עד' must exclude what follows. It can also mean 'including.'

steps.title: Why didn't the משנה just say 'until הללויה'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא: if the משנה meant to include הללויה, it should have said so directly. The difficulty is left unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the משנה say 'until הללויה'! And if you say we wouldn't know which הללויה it meant, let it say 'the הללויה of ״אם הבנים שמחה״.' This is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's reading and ends with 'קשיא', meaning the problem stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה really wanted us to say the word הללויה, naming that word as the stopping point would have been clearer. Even the worry that there are many הללויהs is not a good excuse, because the משנה could have said 'the הללויה of ״אם הבנים שמחה״.' רב חסדא's reading therefore looks forced.

keyTerms.meaning: it is difficult (the challenge stands unanswered)

steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' here is not a complete refutation like 'תיובתא.' It only means the question has no answer at this point.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's view, that הללויה ends a chapter, has trouble with the משנה's wording.

phrases.english: Then let it say 'until "Halleluyah"'!
And if you say that we would not know which 'Halleluyah' —
then let it say 'the "Halleluyah" of "A joyful mother of children"'?
It is difficult.
phrases.notes: The challenge stands

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's explanation from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's reading of the משנה as 'until and including.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה meant to include הללויה, it should have named it directly. It could even have said 'the הללויה of ״אם הבנים שמחה״.'

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא: everyone agrees הללויה begins a chapter
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא reads both sources as agreeing that הללויה starts a chapter, explaining 'until' as 'until but not including.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא explains it according to his own view: everyone holds that הללויה is the start of a chapter. The one who says 'until ״אם הבנים שמחה״' is fine. The one who says 'until ״בצאת ישראל״' holds that 'until' does not include the end point.
steps.whatsHappening: A second way to reject the proof from step 1. Here הללויה belongs to the next chapter, so neither source says it before the meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה בר רב הונא, the משנה's 'until ״אם הבנים שמחה״' is perfectly accurate. The ברייתא's 'until ״בצאת ישראל״' must then mean you stop just before the next chapter, which begins with הללויה. This time the forced reading falls on the ברייתא's wording, not the משנה's. The next step challenges it.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא make the משנה and the ברייתא agree. They differ only on where הללויה belongs, and that shapes how each reads the word 'עד.' Each reading forces one source's wording, and the next step shows that each is left with a קשיא.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna explains it according to his reasoning:
that according to everyone, 'Halleluyah' is the start of a chapter,

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר עַד ״אֵם הַבָּנִים שְׂמֵחָה״ — שַׁפִּיר,
phrases.english: the one who says 'until "A joyful mother of children"' is fine,
and the one who says 'until "When Israel came forth"',
holds: 'until', and the end point is not included.
phrases.notes: So you stop before the הללויה that opens the next chapter

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a parallel rejection of step 1, using the opposite view of where הללויה belongs.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that the משנה and the ברייתא argue.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'עד' can mean 'not including,' so the ברייתא's ״בצאת ישראל״ can mark a stop before the next chapter's opening הללויה.

steps.title: Challenging the 'until but not including' reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks רבה בר רב הונא the same kind of question it asked רב חסדא. If the ברייתא meant to stop before the הללויה, it should have said 'until הללויה', or 'until the הללויה of בצאת ישראל'. The difficulty is left unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the ברייתא just say 'until הללויה'. And if you say we would not know which הללויה it means, let it say 'until the הללויה of בצאת ישראל'. This is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks רבה בר רב הונא's explanation, just as it attacked רב חסדא's in step 3. It ends with 'קשיא', which means the problem stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר רב הונא said the ברייתא's 'until ״בצאת ישראל״' means 'up to, but not including', so you stop before the הללויה that begins the next chapter. The גמרא asks why the ברייתא did not just name that הללויה as its stopping point. If there was a worry about which הללויה was meant, it could have said 'the one of בצאת ישראל'.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him say (why did the ברייתא not word it this way?)
And if you will say (introduces a possible defense)
'When Israel went out', the chapter of הלל that follows

steps.whatToRemember: Both explanations of 'until', the one of רב חסדא and the one of רבה בר רב הונא, end with an unanswered קשיא. רב חסדא's reading strains the משנה's wording, and רבה בר רב הונא's strains the ברייתא's.

phrases.english: Then let him say: 'until halleluya'.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא could have named the stopping point directly.

phrases.english: And if you say that we would not know which halleluya is meant,
phrases.notes: A possible defense: there are several הללויה's in הלל.

phrases.english: then let him say: 'until the halleluya of When Israel went out'!
phrases.notes: According to רבה בר רב הונא, this הללויה opens the next chapter.

phrases.english: It is difficult.
phrases.notes: The question is left unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in step 4, in the same way step 3 attacked step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב הונא's reading of the ברייתא's 'until ״בצאת ישראל״' as 'until but not including'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא meant to stop just before the הללויה that opens בצאת ישראל, the clearest wording would name that הללויה directly. The ברייתא's indirect wording does not fit this reading.

steps.title: Past tense in the redemption blessing, present tense in prayer
steps.stepSummary: Explaining the משנה's words 'וחותם בגאולה', רבא says that קריאת שמע and הלל end with 'גאל ישראל' (past tense), while תפילה ends with 'גואל ישראל' (present tense), because תפילה is a request for mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he ends with redemption.' רבא said: in קריאת שמע and הלל, the blessing is 'Who redeemed Israel'. In תפילה, it is 'Who redeems Israel'. What is the reason? Because תפילה is a request for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase in the משנה, 'וחותם בגאולה'. רבא then explains how the redemption blessing is worded in different places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After קריאת שמע and over the cup at the סדר, we thank ה׳ for the redemption that already happened, so the blessing uses the past tense, 'גאל'. In שמונה עשרה we are asking for redemption that is still ongoing and still to come, so the blessing uses 'גואל'. The tense of the blessing follows its purpose: praise looks back, while a request for רחמים looks forward.

keyTerms.meaning: And he ends (the closing words of a blessing)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why our סידור has 'גאל ישראל' after קריאת שמע but 'גואל ישראל' in שמונה עשרה. The wording of a blessing depends on whether it praises or requests.

phrases.english: And he concludes with redemption.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, introducing the new topic.

phrases.english: Rava said:
For the Shema and hallel: 'Who redeemed Israel.'
phrases.notes: Past tense.

phrases.english: For prayer: 'Who redeems Israel.'
phrases.notes: Present tense, ongoing.

phrases.english: What is the reason? Because it is a request for mercy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'until הללויה' debate and opens a new topic from the next words of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blessings of praise for past redemption say 'גאל ישראל'. The תפילה, which is a request for mercy, says 'גואל ישראל'.

steps.title: Past tense in קידוש, request form in prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא gives a parallel example. קידוש says 'אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו' (Who sanctified us, past tense), while תפילה says 'קדשנו במצותיך' (sanctify us, a request), because תפילה is a request for mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: in קידוש we say 'Who sanctified us with His מצוות and commanded us'. In תפילה we say 'Sanctify us with Your מצוות'. What is the reason? Because תפילה is a request for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא adds a second example of the same rule that רבא taught. This time the example is about the words for holiness instead of the words for redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידוש describes something ה׳ already did, so it is in the past tense and speaks about ה׳ as 'He'. In תפילה we ask ה׳ directly, 'You', to make us holy, so it is phrased as a request. The same reason is repeated word for word, 'דרחמי נינהו', which shows this is one rule seen in two places.

keyTerms.meaning: קידוש, the blessing that declares the day holy
Because it is a request for mercy

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
For kiddush: 'Who sanctified us with His מצוות and commanded us.'
phrases.notes: Past tense, speaking about ה׳ as 'He'.

phrases.english: For prayer: 'Sanctify us with Your מצוות.'
phrases.notes: A request, speaking to ה׳ directly as 'You'.

phrases.english: What is the reason? Because it is a request for mercy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel example of רבא's principle, using the same structure and the same reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידוש uses the past tense, 'אשר קדשנו'. The תפילה uses a request, 'קדשנו במצותיך', because it asks for mercy.

steps.title: Mentioning the Exodus in קידוש
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב rules that קידוש must mention יציאת מצרים. He learns this from a comparison of two פסוקים that share the words 'remember' and 'day'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: one must mention יציאת מצרים in the קידוש of the day. It is written here: 'So that you will remember the day' (that you left Egypt). And it is written there: 'Remember the day of שבת to make it holy'.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the topic of קידוש, רב אחא בר יעקב teaches a new rule. קידוש must include a mention of יציאת מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about פסח says to remember 'the day' you left Egypt. The פסוק about שבת says to remember 'the day' of שבת to sanctify it. Because the two פסוקים share the same language, a גזירה שוה connects them, so remembering the Exodus becomes part of sanctifying the day in קידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here... and it is written there (the setup of a גזירה שוה)
Learning one law from another because two פסוקים use the same word

steps.confusionAlert: 'Here' (הכא) means the פסוק about פסח and יציאת מצרים. 'There' (התם) means the פסוק about שבת. The law moves from the פסח verse onto the שבת קידוש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the words 'זכר ליציאת מצרים' that we say in קידוש every שבת, even though שבת is not directly about the Exodus.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
And one must mention the exodus from Egypt
in the kiddush of the day.
It is written here: 'That you may remember the day.'
phrases.notes: דברים טז:ג, about leaving Egypt.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״זָכוֹר אֶת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת לְקַדְּשׁוֹ״.
phrases.english: And it is written there: 'Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it.'
phrases.notes: שמות כ:ח. The shared words link the two פסוקים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: וְצָרִיךְ שֶׁיַּזְכִּיר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם בְּקִידּוּשׁ הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with the topic of קידוש from step 7 and adds a new requirement for what it must contain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידוש must include a mention of יציאת מצרים. This is derived through a גזירה שוה between the פסוק of remembering the day of the Exodus and the פסוק of remembering the day of שבת to sanctify it.

steps.title: Two more blessing endings: the daily prayer and the הפטרה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שילא states that the ברכה in תפילה about דוד's kingdom ends 'מצמיח קרן ישועה', while the ברכה after the הפטרה ends 'מגן דוד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שילא said: In the prayer, the ending is 'Who makes the horn of salvation grow'. After the הפטרה, the ending is 'Shield of David'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps listing how ברכות end, continuing from רבא and רבי זירא. רבה בר שילא tells us that two ברכות about דוד end in two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברכות speak about the kingdom of דוד. In the daily תפילה, the ending is a request for the future: 'מצמיח קרן ישועה', 'Who makes salvation grow'. After the הפטרה, the ending praises God as 'מגן דוד', 'the Shield of David'.

keyTerms.meaning: The הפטרה, the reading from the נביאים after the Torah reading
'Who makes the horn of salvation grow', the ending of the ברכה of 'את צמח דוד'
'Shield of David', the ending of a ברכה after the הפטרה

steps.confusionAlert: 'מגן דוד' here is the ending of a ברכה, a description of God as דוד's protector. It has nothing to do with the six-pointed star shape.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Sheila said:
The one of the prayer ends: 'Who makes the horn of salvation grow',
phrases.notes: The ברכה in שמונה עשרה about the kingdom of דוד.

phrases.english: The one of the haftara ends: 'Shield of David'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of statements about exact ברכה wording, begun by רבא and רבי זירא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In תפילה the דוד ברכה ends 'מצמיח קרן ישועה'; after the הפטרה it ends 'מגן דוד'.

steps.title: A verse hinting to the ending 'Shield of David'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that God's promise to דוד, 'I will make you a great name like the great ones', is fulfilled when we say 'מגן דוד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And I will make for you a great name, like the name of the great ones.' רב יוסף taught: This is what people say, 'Shield of David'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for the ending 'מגן דוד' it just mentioned. רב יוסף connects it to a promise God made to דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'great ones' are the אבות, and a ברכה already ends with 'מגן אברהם'. When the ברכה after the הפטרה ends with 'מגן דוד', דוד's name is placed in a ברכה ending just like אברהם's. That is how his name became 'like the name of the great ones'.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught (a teaching of the תנאים, a ברייתא)
Like the name of the great ones (the אבות)
This is what people say, meaning the verse is fulfilled in this wording

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why דוד, out of everyone after the אבות, gets his own ברכה ending: the פסוק promised him a name like theirs.

phrases.english: 'And I will make for you a great name,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב ז:ט, God's promise to דוד through נתן הנביא.

phrases.english: like the name of the great ones',
Rav Yosef taught:
This is what they say: 'Shield of David'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for the ending 'מגן דוד' mentioned in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ending 'מגן דוד' fulfills the promise 'כשם הגדולים'.

steps.title: God's blessing to אברהם hints to the three forefathers in the prayer
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads three parts of God's blessing to אברהם as matching 'God of אברהם, God of יצחק, God of יעקב' in the first ברכה of תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: 'And I will make you a great nation' is fulfilled when we say 'God of אברהם'. 'And I will bless you' is fulfilled when we say 'God of יצחק'. 'And I will make your name great' is fulfilled when we say 'God of יעקב'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק that hints to wording in תפילה. ריש לקיש matches three phrases of God's promise to אברהם with the three names of the אבות at the start of שמונה עשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God promised אברהם three things, and each one comes true through the opening words of תפילה. Even mentioning יצחק and יעקב counts as a blessing to אברהם, because a father is honored when his son and grandson are remembered. This sets up the next step, which asks how the ברכה should end.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And I will make you a great nation' (בראשית יב:ב)
'And I will make your name great'
'God of אברהם', the opening words of the first ברכה of תפילה

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
'And I will make you a great nation',
phrases.notes: בראשית יב:ב.

phrases.english: this is what they say: 'God of Avraham'.
'And I will bless you': this is what they say, 'God of Yitzchak'.
phrases.notes: It is a blessing to a father when his son's name lives on.

phrases.english: 'And I will make your name great',
this is what they say: 'God of Yaakov'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels רב יוסף's reading. A promise to an ancestor is fulfilled through the wording of a ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three opening names in the first ברכה of תפילה fulfill three parts of God's blessing to אברהם.

steps.title: The first blessing ends with אברהם alone
steps.stepSummary: One might think the ברכה should end by mentioning all three אבות. The words 'והיה ברכה' teach that it ends with אברהם alone, which is why we say 'מגן אברהם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think we should end the blessing with all of them. So the verse says: 'And you shall be a blessing.' With you, אברהם, the blessing ends. It does not end with all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes ריש לקיש's reading of the פסוק. The last phrase, 'והיה ברכה', teaches how the first ברכה of תפילה ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because all three אבות open the ברכה, we might think all three should also appear in its ending. 'והיה ברכה' ('you shall be a blessing') is said to אברהם alone. So he alone appears in the ending, 'ברוך אתה ה׳ מגן אברהם'.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (introduces a wrong assumption that a פסוק will correct)
End the ברכה (the חתימה, the closing 'ברוך אתה ה׳' line)

steps.whatToRemember: The first ברכה of תפילה opens with all three אבות but ends only with 'מגן אברהם'. This is learned from 'והיה ברכה', meaning 'with you, אברהם, the ברכה ends'. The ברכה after the הפטרה ends with 'מגן דוד', so that דוד's name is 'like the great ones'.
steps.confusionAlert: 'יכול' is not a real question from someone in the גמרא. It is a setup that brings up a possible mistaken idea, so the פסוק can show us the correct rule.

phrases.english: One might think they should conclude with all of them?
The verse teaches: 'And you shall be a blessing'.
With you they conclude,
and they do not conclude with all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יְהוּ חוֹתְמִין בְּכוּלָּן תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes ריש לקיש's reading by using the last phrase of the same פסוק to set the ending of the ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first ברכה of תפילה ends with אברהם alone ('מגן אברהם'), not with all three אבות.

steps.title: רבא reports the practice of the סבי דפומבדיתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells us that the סבי דפומבדיתא held that תפילה and קידוש end the same way. On שבת both end 'מקדש השבת'. On יום טוב both end 'מקדש ישראל והזמנים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I found the סבי דפומבדיתא sitting and saying: On שבת, both in תפילה and in קידוש, we say 'Who sanctifies שבת.' On יום טוב, both in תפילה and in קידוש, we say 'Who sanctifies ישראל and the seasons.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reports the opinion of the סבי דפומבדיתא about how the closing ברכה of תפילה and קידוש should be worded. This sets up his own disagreement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In their view, the ending depends only on the day, not on whether it is תפילה or קידוש. שבת gets 'מקדש השבת'. יום טוב gets 'מקדש ישראל והזמנים'.

keyTerms.meaning: The Elders of Pumbedita, older scholars of the city of Pumbedita
קידוש, the blessing over wine that declares the day holy
Who sanctifies ישראל and the seasons (the festivals)

phrases.english: Rava said:
I found the Elders of Pumbedita
sitting and saying:
On Shabbat, both in prayer and in kiddush:
"Who sanctifies Shabbat."

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹמָא טָבָא — בֵּין בִּצְלוֹתָא וּבֵין בְּקִידּוּשָׁא:
phrases.english: On a Festival, both in prayer and in kiddush:
"Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַשְׁכַּחְתִּינָא לְסָבֵי דְפוּמְבְּדִיתָא דְּיָתְבִי וְקָאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of how ברכות end (steps 9–12) and moves to the endings of קידוש and תפילה on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the סבי דפומבדיתא, on שבת both תפילה and קידוש end 'מקדש השבת', and on יום טוב both end 'מקדש ישראל והזמנים'.

steps.title: רבא's opposing ruling: prayer always ends 'Who sanctifies Israel'
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees about תפילה. On both שבת and יום טוב, תפילה ends 'מקדש ישראל'. For קידוש he agrees with the elders: 'מקדש השבת' on שבת and 'מקדש ישראל והזמנים' on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I said to them: On the contrary! In תפילה, on both שבת and יום טוב, we say 'Who sanctifies ישראל.' In the קידוש of שבת we say 'Who sanctifies שבת.' On יום טוב we say 'Who sanctifies ישראל and the seasons.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tells the elders that he holds differently. In his view, the wording depends on whether it is תפילה or קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is only about תפילה. On שבת the elders say 'מקדש השבת', and רבא says 'מקדש ישראל'. On יום טוב the elders say 'מקדש ישראל והזמנים', and רבא says just 'מקדש ישראל'. For קידוש, both sides agree.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite is true

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא disagrees about everything. For קידוש he says exactly what the elders said. The argument is mainly about the ending of תפילה.

phrases.english: And I said to them:
On the contrary, in prayer —
both on Shabbat and on a Festival:
"Who sanctifies Israel";
in the kiddush of Shabbat: "Who sanctifies Shabbat";
on a Festival: "Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing ruling to the view of the סבי דפומבדיתא from step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפילה on both שבת and יום טוב ends 'מקדש ישראל'. קידוש ends 'מקדש השבת' on שבת and 'מקדש ישראל והזמנים' on יום טוב.

steps.title: רבא explains the elders' reasoning: who fixes the holy day
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the elders' reason. שבת is fixed and permanent, so it is not ישראל who makes it holy, and we say 'מקדש השבת'. ישראל set the dates of יום טוב by adding days to months and adding months to years, so we mention ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I can say my reason and your reason. Your reason: שבת is fixed and stays in place, so in both תפילה and קידוש we say 'Who sanctifies שבת.' יום טוב is set by ישראל, who add days to months and fix the years, so we say 'Who sanctifies ישראל and the seasons.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא announces that he will give the reasons for both opinions. He starts with the reason behind the elders' view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The elders' logic is about who makes the day holy. שבת comes every seventh day on its own, so ישראל have no part in making it holy. The date of יום טוב depends on בית דין setting the calendar, so ישראל are mentioned as the ones who make it holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixed and permanent (שבת always comes on the seventh day)
They add days to months (making a month 30 days instead of 29)
They fix the years (for example, by adding a leap month)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why יום טוב ברכות mention ישראל: the holiness of the festivals passes through the people who set the calendar.

phrases.english: And I can say
my reason and your reason.
Your reason:
Shabbat, which is fixed and permanent —
both in prayer and in kiddush: "Who sanctifies Shabbat."

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא טָבָא, דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא דְּקָבְעִי לֵיהּ —
phrases.english: A Festival, which it is Israel who establish it —
for they add days to months and fix the years:
"Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנָא אָמֵינָא טַעְמָא דִידִי וְטַעְמָא דִידְכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the elders' ruling from step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The elders' view rests on who makes the day holy: God fixed שבת, and ישראל set the festivals.

steps.title: רבא's own reasoning: public prayer versus individual kiddush
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains his view. תפילה is said in a group, so it ends 'מקדש ישראל' in honor of the community. קידוש is said by an individual, so on שבת it ends 'מקדש השבת', and on יום טוב 'מקדש ישראל והזמנים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: My reason: תפילה is said in a group, so we say 'Who sanctifies ישראל.' קידוש is said by an individual, so on שבת we say 'Who sanctifies שבת,' and on יום טוב 'Who sanctifies ישראל and the seasons.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the reason for his own opinion from step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the key question is whether the ברכה is said by the community or by one person. When the community is gathered, we mention ישראל to honor them. In קידוש, said by one person, we go back to the elders' logic of who makes the day holy.

keyTerms.meaning: In a group; with the community

phrases.english: My reason:
Prayer, which is in public:
"Who sanctifies Israel."
Kiddush, which is by an individual,
on Shabbat: "Who sanctifies Shabbat";
on a Festival: "Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's promise in step 15 by giving his own reason, which supports his ruling in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Group תפילה mentions ישראל. Individual קידוש mentions what makes the day holy: שבת itself, or ישראל who set the festivals.

steps.title: Challenge: prayer can be alone and kiddush can be in public
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's reasoning. People sometimes pray alone, and קידוש is sometimes said in a group, so the difference between group and individual does not hold up.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so! Is there no such thing as תפילה said alone? And is there no such thing as קידוש said in a group?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's reasoning from step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reasoning depends on תפילה being a group activity and קידוש being an individual one. The גמרא points out that this is not always true. Someone can pray at home alone, and קידוש is also said in shul in front of everyone. So the distinction seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so (an objection)

phrases.english: But that is not so:
Is there not prayer by an individual?
And is there not kiddush in public?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, צְלוֹתָא בְּיָחִיד מִי לֵיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reasoning from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's distinction that תפילה is a group activity and קידוש is an individual one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The distinction is not consistent in practice: תפילה can be said alone, and קידוש can be said in a group.

steps.title: רבא's answer: follow the main, typical way it is done
steps.stepSummary: רבא's view is defended. We look at the usual, main form of each one. תפילה is mainly a group activity, and קידוש is mainly the duty of each person at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא holds: go after the main way it is done.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining רבא's principle. The rule is based on how each one is normally done, not on unusual cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא admits that sometimes people pray alone and sometimes קידוש is said in public. But the wording of a ברכה is set by its main, basic form. תפילה is mainly with the community, and קידוש is mainly the individual's own obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: Go after the main thing (follow the typical, main form)

steps.whatToRemember: The elders base the ending on who makes the day holy (God for שבת, ישראל for יום טוב). רבא bases it on group versus individual: תפילה says 'מקדש ישראל', and קידוש follows what makes the day holy. When challenged, רבא follows the main, typical form of each (זיל בתר עיקר).

phrases.english: And Rava holds:
Go after the main thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 17 and defends רבא's reasoning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Principle-based defense: the rule follows the typical case, not the exceptions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because תפילה is sometimes said alone and קידוש sometimes in public, רבא's group-versus-individual distinction seemed to fall apart.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording follows the main nature of each: תפילה is basically communal, and קידוש is basically individual.

steps.title: רבא stays silent when עולא בר רב follows the elders
steps.stepSummary: עולא בר רב led the prayers in front of רבא using the wording of סבי דפומבדיתא. רבא said nothing, which shows רבא changed his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא בר רב went down to lead the prayers in front of רבא. He said the ending the way סבי דפומבדיתא say it, and רבא did not say anything to him. This shows that רבא changed his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story to show that רבא gave up his own view about how to end the תפילה and accepted the view of סבי דפומבדיתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 14, רבא held that תפילה should always end 'מקדש ישראל'. Here a prayer leader used the elders' wording in front of him, and he did not correct him. The גמרא reads his silence as agreement, so רבא must have taken back his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Went down before him, meaning he led the prayers. The prayer leader's spot was lower than the rest of the room.
He retracted, he changed his mind

steps.confusionAlert: 'נחית' does not mean he went downstairs for no reason. It is the standard phrase for leading the prayers, because the חזן stood in a lower spot.

phrases.aramaic: עוּלָּא בַּר רַב נְחֵית קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא,
phrases.english: Ulla bar Rav went down (to lead prayers) before Rava,
he said it like the Elders of Pumbedita,
and he (Rava) did not say anything at all to him.
phrases.notes: רבא's silence is the key evidence.

phrases.english: Apparently, Rava retracted (his view).
phrases.notes: The גמרא's conclusion from the silence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבא's reasoning in Step 18, the גמרא now shows through a story that רבא himself later accepted the elders' view.
steps.raayaObject: That רבא retracted and accepted the wording of סבי דפומבדיתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא stayed silent when עולא בר רב led the prayers using the elders' wording

steps.title: רב פפא praises a leader who follows the elders
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן led the prayers before רב פפא using the elders' wording, and רב פפא praised him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן, the father of רב הונא בריה דרב נתן, went down to lead the prayers in front of רב פפא. He said it like סבי דפומבדיתא, and רב פפא praised him.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story shows that a later אמורא actively approved of the elders' wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes one step past Step 19. There the evidence was only silence. Here רב פפא openly praised the leader, which is stronger support that the elders' wording is correct.

phrases.english: Rav Natan, the father of Rav Huna
son of Rav Natan,
phrases.notes: This is the full name of the son, 'רב הונא בריה דרב נתן'.

phrases.english: went down (to lead prayers) before Rav Pappa,
he said it like the Elders of Pumbedita,
and Rav Pappa praised him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story that adds stronger support (open praise rather than silence) for the elders' view.
steps.raayaObject: That the elders' wording is the correct practice
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב פפא openly praised a prayer leader who used it

steps.title: מרימר rules that the הלכה follows the elders
steps.stepSummary: רבינא saw a prayer leader in סורא use the elders' wording. The people tried to quiet him, but מרימר told them the הלכה follows סבי דפומבדיתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: I happened to come to סורא, to מרימר. The שליח ציבור went down to lead the prayers in front of him and said it like סבי דפומבדיתא. Everyone was trying to quiet him. מרימר said to them: Leave him alone. The הלכה follows סבי דפומבדיתא. Then they stopped trying to quiet him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the topic with an open ruling: the הלכה follows סבי דפומבדיתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people in סורא were used to a different wording, so the elders' version sounded wrong to them. מרימר stopped them and said plainly 'הילכתא', the הלכה. This turns the earlier hints from Steps 19 and 20 into a clear final ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Were silencing, trying to quiet him

steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה follows סבי דפומבדיתא. On שבת, both the תפילה and the קידוש end 'מקדש השבת'. On יום טוב, both end 'מקדש ישראל והזמנים'. רבא's split between תפילה and קידוש is not followed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why our סידור uses the same ending in תפילה and in קידוש: 'מקדש השבת' on שבת and 'מקדש ישראל והזמנים' on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Ravina said: I happened to come to Sura
before Mareimar,
and the prayer leader went down before him
and said it like the Elders of Pumbedita,
and everyone was trying to silence him,
phrases.notes: In Sura they were not used to this wording.

phrases.english: He (Mareimar) said to them: Leave him,
the halacha follows the Elders of Pumbedita,
phrases.notes: The final ruling.

phrases.english: and they no longer silenced him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the two earlier stories and states the final הלכה outright.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows סבי דפומבדיתא. On שבת, both תפילה and קידוש end 'מקדש השבת'. On יום טוב, both end 'מקדש ישראל והזמנים'.

steps.title: משנה: the third and fourth cups and drinking between cups
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says ברכת המזון is said over the third cup. הלל is finished over the fourth cup, along with ברכת השיר. One may drink between the first cups, but not between the third and the fourth.
steps.simpleTranslation: They poured him the third cup, and he says the ברכה over his food (ברכת המזון). Over the fourth cup he finishes הלל and says ברכת השיר. Between these cups, if he wants to drink, he may drink. But between the third and the fourth cup, he should not drink.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes what happens with the last two of the ארבע כוסות at the סדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives each cup a job: the third cup goes with ברכת המזון, and the fourth cup goes with the rest of הלל and ברכת השיר. It also sets a rule: extra wine is allowed between the earlier cups, but not between the third and fourth.

keyTerms.meaning: He blesses over his food, meaning ברכת המזון
Finishes הלל. The first part was said before the meal.
The blessing of song said at the end of הלל

steps.confusionAlert: 'גומר את הלל' means finishing הלל, not saying all of it now. The first part was already said earlier in the סדר.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
They poured for him the third cup;
he recites the blessing over his food (Grace After Meals).
(Over the) fourth, he completes hallel,
and says over it the blessing of the song.
Between these cups,
if he wants to drink, he may drink;
between the third and the fourth, he should not drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה and a new topic. The earlier discussion about ברכה endings is over.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת המזון is said over the third cup. הלל is finished and ברכת השיר is said over the fourth cup. Drinking is allowed between the earlier cups but not between the third and fourth.

steps.title: רב חנן: ברכת המזון needs a cup of wine
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן tries to prove from the משנה that ברכת המזון always requires a כוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן said to רבא: We can learn from this that ברכת המזון needs a cup of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב חנן drawing a general rule from the משנה: since the משנה puts ברכת המזון on a cup, ברכת המזון must always require a cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנן's logic is this: if the משנה links the third cup to ברכת המזון, a cup must be a basic requirement of ברכת המזון. That would apply all year, not only at the סדר. This sets up רבא's reply in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, this proves that

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Chanan said to Rava:
Learn from it
(that) Grace After Meals requires a cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן טְעוּנָה כּוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from the משנה just quoted.
steps.raayaObject: That ברכת המזון always requires a cup of wine
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה, which says ברכת המזון is said over the third cup

steps.title: רבא: each of the four cups was simply given a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof. חז"ל set up four cups as a sign of freedom, and then attached a מצוה to each one. That does not show that ברכת המזון needs a cup all year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: חז"ל set up four cups as a way of showing freedom. Since we already have them, we do a מצוה with each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב חנן's proof and shows that the משנה does not teach what רב חנן claimed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four cups exist because of חירות (freedom), not because of ברכת המזון. Once the four cups were in place, חז"ל gave each one a job, and ברכת המזון was one of them. So the third cup belongs to the סדר, and this proves nothing about ברכת המזון on other days.

keyTerms.meaning: In the manner of freedom, as free people do

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say that ברכת המזון never needs a cup. He only says this משנה is not proof of it, because the cup here comes from the four cups of the סדר.
steps.whatToRemember: A rule that applies at the סדר cannot automatically be turned into a rule for the whole year. The four cups come from חירות, and their pairing with ברכת המזון is only a way to use them for a מצוה.

phrases.english: He (Rava) said to him:
The Rabbis instituted four cups
in the manner of freedom,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל חַד וְחַד נַעֲבֵיד בֵּיהּ מִצְוָה.
phrases.english: (so) with each and every one, we perform a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְבַּע כָּסֵי תִּיקְּנוּ רַבָּנַן דֶּרֶךְ חֵירוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects רב חנן's proof from Step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. It makes no final ruling on whether ברכת המזון needs a cup in general.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The third cup exists because of the four cups of חירות, not because ברכת המזון needs a cup. Attaching a מצוה to each cup was a later add-on and shows nothing about the rest of the year.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on the fourth cup
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-quotes the משנה: over the fourth cup one finishes הלל and says ברכת השיר. This opens a new discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Over the fourth cup, he finishes הלל and says ברכת השיר over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes one line from the משנה about the fourth cup. This is a setup line that prepares the next question: what exactly is 'ברכת השיר'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion was about the third cup and whether ברכת המזון needs a כוס. Now the גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה, the fourth cup. The משנה says to say a 'blessing of song' but does not say which blessing. That open question is what the גמרא will deal with next.

keyTerms.meaning: The fourth cup of the סדר
הלל, the psalms of praise. Part is said before the meal and the rest is finished here.
Over it, meaning over the cup
'The blessing of song,' a closing blessing said after הלל. Its exact identity is discussed next.

steps.confusionAlert: This line also appeared in step 22. The גמרא is not just repeating itself. It is quoting the משנה again to start a new topic, which is the meaning of ברכת השיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer to 'what is ברכת השיר' decides what we actually say at the end of הלל at the סדר.

phrases.english: Over the fourth cup, he completes the Hallel
phrases.notes: The first part of הלל was said before the meal. Here it is finished.

phrases.english: and he says over it the blessing of song.
phrases.notes: The משנה does not say which blessing this is. That is the next question.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה (as the opening of the coming question about ברכת השיר)
steps.triggerLanguage: רְבִיעִי גּוֹמֵר עָלָיו אֶת הַהַלֵּל וְאוֹמֵר עָלָיו בִּרְכַּת הַשִּׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's דחיה closed the third-cup discussion, the גמרא moves on to the next clause of the משנה, about the fourth cup.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Over the fourth cup, one finishes הלל and recites ברכת השיר.
